# Native linked credential dispatch source handoff

This packet restores product-backed environment dispatch for current linked credentials only when the actual default credential authority and the owning native PostgreSQL handle prove the same immutable opening target. It also corrects the APPLY publication regression: an infrastructure.plan operation may retain original read-only custody for a current tenant viewer. Publication and claim reservation do not grant provider writes. Ordinary apply still requires editor or admin membership and the current write credential scope. A delegated destroy retains its viewer requester only through the canonical immutable teardown-review proposal, the actual evaluated system teardown-review requirement, current planning scope, and at least one current admin browser approval.

The nine owned paths are the hosted PostgreSQL client, PostgreSQL credential authority, current integration grant directory, worker broker, native product authority helper, descriptor-safe opener membership, two new native suites, and this handoff. Preparation is the exact read-only APPLY candidate tree 15a7dad7a0bc2a3fb483a9c5cdefbdbeda217a23 on d5b68107319aa509e86352aab2fb6bd15e47abe6. Its existing WeakMap membership now checks each of kind, identity, query, tx, exec and close through own data descriptors, preserving exact methods and synchronous close invalidation without invoking substituted getters.

A tooling constructor, structural copy, supplied SQL closure, global replacement, accessor, closed client or changed default selection cannot originate the new dispatch proof. It never selects token_hash, encrypted link material, bearer values or free-form metadata in that read. It attaches the original private tuple to the genuine evaluated worker snapshot before any approving-human role await. A copied tuple or dispatch snapshot cannot supply this origin.

Claimed, dispatched, uncertain, original binary custody, existing leases, plan integrity, source recipes and non-replay transitions remain in their canonical repositories.
